paragraphs.source_en: If the three carp Nobunaga had sent—representing himself, his son-in-law Nobuyasu, and his kinsman by marriage Ieyasu—had been cooked and eaten by Ieyasu's retainers, who had then all drunk themselves senseless... someone must have directed them, and there had to be some deeper meaning behind it.
